questions.def: 'Because' introduces an adverbial clause of reason.
questions.question: ___ it rained, we stayed home.

questions.def: 'When' introduces an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I arrive.

questions.def: 'After' introduces an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: He will go ___ he has finished.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a conditional adverbial clause.
questions.question: ___ I study hard, I will pass the exam.

questions.def: 'Wherever' introduces an adverbial clause of place.
questions.question: She can go ___ she wants to.

questions.def: 'As' introduces an adverbial clause of manner.
questions.question: ___ he works, he earns money.

questions.def: 'Until' introduces an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: I will wait ___ you are ready.

questions.def: 'Although' introduces a clause of concession.
questions.question: ___ he is rich, he is not happy.

questions.def: Use the present simple after 'while' when referring to the future.
questions.question: While I am waiting, I will read a book.

questions.def: 'Wherever' introduces an adverbial clause of place.
questions.question: They ___ they want.

questions.def: 'Than' is used in comparative adverbial clauses.
questions.question: She is taller ___ her sister.

questions.def: 'As fast as' introduces a clause of manner.
questions.question: He runs ___ he can.

questions.def: 'When' introduces an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I have time.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a conditional adverbial clause.
questions.question: He will pass ___ he studies.

questions.def: 'Even though' introduces a clause of concession.
questions.question: ___ he was tired, he continued.

questions.def: Use the present simple in adverbial clauses of time referring to the future.
questions.question: I will give it to him when I will see him.

questions.def: 'As' introduces an adverbial clause of manner.

questions.def: 'When' introduces an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: She started ___ the bell rang.

questions.def: 'If' introduces a conditional clause.
questions.question: ___ he studies, he will pass.

questions.def: 'Because' introduces an adverbial clause of reason.

questions.def: 'When' introduces an adverbial clause of time.
questions.question: I will leave ___ you are ready.

questions.def: 'As' introduces an adverbial clause of manner.
questions.question: He drives ___ he is careful.

questions.question: I will call you ___ I arrive.

questions.def: 'Wherever' clause of place.
questions.question: She can sing ___ she wants to.

questions.def: 'Even if' introduces a clause of concession.
questions.question: ___ he is tired, he works.

questions.def: "When" introduces an adverbial clause of time. It indicates when the action will happen.
questions.question: I will call you ___ I arrive home.

questions.def: "After" indicates the sequence of events. Cooking started after arrival.
questions.question: She started cooking ___ he got home.

questions.def: "After I eat lunch" is an adverbial clause of time. 'Shopping' is the correct use.
questions.question: I will go ___ after I ___ lunch.

questions.def: "If" introduces a condition. She'll pass *if* she studies.
questions.question: ___ she studies hard, she will pass the exam.

questions.def: "Although" introduces a contrasting idea (it was late, but we walked).
questions.question: ___ it was late, we decided to walk home.
